business: REPAIHUB: online service that moves money from an Indian NRO account to a Canadian bank account, with the Indian tax forms and CA certificate handled
by_segment: Settled mid-career professional with old FDs, rent or savings in NRO (₹5L-₹20L)
Newer immigrant (PR < 5 yrs) with modest NRO balance (under ₹5L)
Property seller / inheritor with a lump sum (₹20L-₹1Cr waiting in NRO)
Retiree / parent-age with Indian pension or rental income (₹3L-₹15L a year)
why_not: I only move money through my own bank's NRI desk, and I would not hand my NRO savings to a brand-new company that is still waiting on its FINTRAC registration. It also is not even launched yet, and I only go to India every couple of years.

I'm not handing a lump sum from a property sale to a company that isn't even FINTRAC-registered yet and can't launch till 2027. My cousin in India already handles this through his CA and I know who I'm dealing with.
My NRO money has sat there for years and I keep telling myself I'll sort it on my next trip. It isn't launching until 2027 and I won't act on a waitlist, so a signup now is just a polite maybe.

My cousin in India already handles this for me through his CA, and it costs me next to nothing. Paying about CAD $340 to move 10 lakh doesn't make sense when I earn well and already have a way that works.

About CAD $342 to move ten lakh is a lot when I compare it to Wise or my bank, and my relative in India can handle the paperwork for free. It's also not even launched yet, so there's nothing for me to try.

About CAD $342 to move 10 lakh (317 if first transfer is free) is a lot when my relative in India can handle the paperwork for free, or a CA there charges a few thousand rupees. It is also not launched and FINTRAC is only 'in process', so I would not put savings through it.
flip: FINTRAC registration done, a few real reviews from people who moved a similar amount, and a total fee under about CAD $200 on ₹10 lakh.

My own Indian bank or a big Canadian bank endorsing or partnering with it, FINTRAC registration completed, a year or more of track record, and a clear written explanation of the Canadian and Indian tax treatment.
FINTRAC registration actually completed, the named partner bank and CA firm disclosed, and a few months of real track record with transfers of my size.
Several people in my community group saying they moved money with them without trouble, plus FINTRAC registration completed and a clear explanation of the tax filing on both sides.
A total cost under about CAD $120 for ten lakh, plus being fully FINTRAC-registered with real reviews from people I know in my community.
Several people in my community group saying they moved money with them safely, plus FINTRAC registration done and a much lower fee, around 0.5% or less.
FINTRAC registration done, a track record of a year or more, and my own CA confirming the tax treatment and the Form 145/146 filings are correct.

Several people in my community group or temple association vouching that they moved money with them and it arrived, plus the FINTRAC registration completed and confirmation that my Indian bank will not need me to visit.
FINTRAC registration completed, plus the partner bank named and a few reviews from people I know or a community I trust. A lower fee for small amounts would help too.

A fee under about 0.7% with FINTRAC registration done and a track record from real customers. Or if my cousin stopped being able to help.
